reviews.title: Finally, I’m free
reviews.text:
I myself come from a generation that had and now has unfettered access to YouTube, instagram, etc… since its infancy. My mind has developed an extremely obsessive and addictive habit towards these applications, causing me to not even be able to do my bed in the mornings, I have had phases in life when I somewhat restricted my use of social media/gaming/xxx and it led to me completing my bachelors in mathematics and landing a great job, but I was never fully free until now. It has been only 5 days and my screen time is down from 4 hours to less than an 45 minutes a day. This focus had led to me being so productive I completed projects that I previously thought were going to take weeks in days. 

I dabbled with other methods such as screen time passcode and assistive access. But assistive access genuinely limited some important tools in communication I needed and screen time passcode required me to have my fiancée constantly on call just in case I needed to search something up or use the internet. 

This in app allows me to set a clear boundary between using technology for my benefit, versus using it as an escape for my boredom.

Thank for giving me my life back.

reviews.title: Great App, Broken Upgrade Process
reviews.text:
I actually like Jomo and decided to upgrade to the Lifetime plan because I believe in the app. Unfortunately, the upgrade process is poorly designed. The app instructs users to purchase the Lifetime plan first and then request a refund from Apple for the annual subscription. I followed those instructions exactly, but Apple denied my refund request. As a result, I ended up paying for both an Annual subscription and a Lifetime subscription.

If this upgrade path depends on Apple approving refunds, it’s not a reliable system. Jomo should redesign the upgrade process so customers aren’t put in this situation. For example, they could offer the Lifetime purchase through their website, provide a prorated upgrade, or use another method that doesn’t rely on Apple’s refund process.

I still think the app is great, but the upgrade experience left me frustrated. I hope the developers improve this so future customers don’t end up paying twice.

reviews.title: Exactly what I need: external support
reviews.text: I’ve tried to write a longer, fancier, nicer, more detailed review of Jomo but my app always kicks me out or something before I can hit send. Willpower didn’t stop my phone addiction; I needed external support. This app does it almost perfectly. Sounds like I’m getting paid for this review, but yes I do actually recommend other people download it — unpopular opinion but everyone of every age will live a better life if we stop doomscrolling and avoiding people.

reviews.title: As an IG addicted 21 year old…
reviews.text:
I love this app. I was using a free trial from Opal, but the $99.99 yearly price tag was a little out of my student budget.

I was also on Instagram for 5-6 hours A DAY… Safe to say I’m a recovering social media addict.

Then I scanned a screen time blocker sub-Reddit and was intrigued by Jomo (especially seeing it’s independently run and woman co-owned). It has a ton of features like continuous app blocking, screen time intention setting, routine building, and more. I can honestly see how the settings could be customized for any routine or lifestyle.

Plus it’s only $29.99 a year compared to $99.99, and mine was only $14.99 with their student discount.

Disclaimer: I’m not a longtime user, only 3 days so far, but I can say that I’ve seen an improvement in my reading time and my presence in conversations, both of which are important in my life.

If you’re on the fence, I’d say just get Jomo. Even if you’re not a fan of every single feature, it’ll help you take some of your time back 🫂💕

reviews.title: It was great until it wasn’t
reviews.text:
This app was incredible at first. There is so much possibility with all the features included, but lately, it’s simply not working. The strict modes, which I think are the only true way to limit usage behavior, aren’t counting time spent. I set 30 minutes of X dot com daily, and i’ll be on it for well over 30 minutes and I think to check on my time usage, and it hasn’t counted a minute. 

In fact, today, it went from locked up, to now I have 15 more minutes of usage. I don’t know what happened with it, but unless It can be fixed, this app is not worth your money. A shame, because it’s far more affordable than Opal, and comes with essentially all the same features. 

I know the devs are a small team, and I am happy to revise my review if things can change, but I am seeing similar reports of the same issues in reviews here. I would love to buy the app outright for lifetime use, but if it’s not going to work as it should, it’s not worth investing $100 into it. 

Hoping things can get better.
